newsitem.title: USA: Florida ruling small victory for Big Tobacco.
newsitem.headline: Florida ruling small victory for Big Tobacco.

text.p: A judge's ruling that limits Florida's drive to recoup hundreds of millions of dollars in Medicaid payments from tobacco companies still leaves the state with room for attack.

While tobacco company lawyers will likely seek similar rulings in other states, other tobacco litigation and potential U.S. Food and Drug Administration reform means the liability burden on tobacco companies is far from being lifted, industry analysts and legal experts said on Tuesday.

A Palm Beach County circuit court judge stripped all but three counts from Florida's 18-count tobacco lawsuit. Florida officials hope to recover more than $400 million a year in Medicaid payments for treatment of tobacco-related illnesses since 1994.
"I think the remaining claims give the states plenty of room to recover some money," said Melissa Ronan, a consultant with Litigation Analysis for Wall Street.
The judge allowed Florida to claim the tobacco industry was negligent and made a dangerous product and ruled the state can seek an injunction to prevent cigarette sales to minors.
Tobacco companies and some analysts called the ruling a significant victory, citing as an example the judge's ruling that Florida had 30 days within which it had to name smokers covered in the suit.
State officials said the names were computerized and readily available. But analysts said confidentiality and verification problems could arise.
"There's only a few things left here (in the Florida suit), which the companies have defended themselves against in the past," said John Maxwell of Wheat First Butcher Singer.
"If they can't come up with the names in 30 days, I think probably the whole case gets thrown out," Maxwell added.
Ronan said, however, she thought the judge would be open to extending the deadline.
The ruling is not likely to dissuade other states from pursuing their suits against tobacco companies.
On Tuesday Illinois said it had decided to sue tobacco companies to recover Medicaid costs. It would be the 16th state to sue the tobacco industry.
"To have the attorneys general jump off the bandwagon, the bandwagon has to clearly slow down," said PaineWebber analyst Emanuel Goldman. "One or two decisions isn't going to do it."
The industry is also facing hundreds of personal-injury suits and class action lawsuits that are weighing on the valuation of tobacco shares.

Nonetheless, tobacco stocks rallied on the Florida news. In afternoon trading, Philip Morris Cos Inc rose 2-3/8 to 94-3/8, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, parent of R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, 1/2 to 27, Loews Corp, parent of Lorillard Tobacco, gained 3/8 to 79-1/8. B.A.T. Industries Plc, parent of Brown & Williamson Tobacco, gained 3/4 to 14-1/2 in U.S. trading.
Smokeless tobacco maker UST Inc added 1-1/2 to 31-1/8.
